title: Discontinuation of statins for primary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in adults aged 75 years or older (SAGA/SITE): a multicentre, open-label, pragmatic, non-inferiority randomised trial
authors: Bonnet F, Poulizac P, Rousselot N, Couffinhal T, Galli G, Berdaï D, et al.
population: People aged 75 or older prescribed a statin for at least 1 year for primary prevention, without atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or dementia, in 297 French primary care offices; median age 80, 66.8% women, 29.5% with diabetes
funder: French Ministry of Health within the framework of the Medico Economical Research Program (PRME) 2014. Registry: sponsor University Hospital, Bordeaux; grant PRME 14-0037 from the French Ministry of Health.
authorConflicts: One author reported non-financial support and personal fees from Gilead, ViiV Healthcare and MSD outside the submitted work; all others declared none.
result: Open-label randomisation 5:4 to continue (639) or stop (521) statins; 1160 analysed for the primary estimand. Death at 36 months: 48 of 604 (7.9%) continuing against 35 of 484 (7.2%) stopping; absolute difference -0.68% (95% CI -3.95 to 2.60), within the prespecified non-inferiority margin of 5%. Adverse events in 461 of 631 (73.1%) continuing and 390 of 527 (74.0%) stopping; non-cardiovascular adverse events 72.3% against 72.7%. The authors conclude that discontinuation was non-inferior to continuation for 3-year all-cause mortality.
